verdict.rationale: Cognee's ingestion pipeline automatically extracts entities and builds a knowledge graph from raw input in one call (docs-16), and the `.improve` operation is documented to enrich the graph and 'bridge short-term session memory into permanent memory' after ingestion, suggesting some background consolidation (docs-31, docs-19). However, both `.remember` and `.improve` are explicitly user/agent-invoked operations rather than an ambient process that autonomously decides what's worth keeping — there's no documented salience-filtering logic, no evidence of the system choosing NOT to remember trivial content, and no evidence of fully automatic background triggering without an explicit call. Missing for 10: autonomous salience/relevance filtering logic, evidence of selective forgetting/skipping of unimportant content, and proof of background consolidation running without explicit invocation.
